Title: Malaysia, Thailand to finalise Sungai Golok project to solve Kelantan, southern Thailand floods
Article:
KOTA BARU: Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Sungai Golok estuary project within a month to help mitigate flooding in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had had two rounds of discussions with the Thai government, including with its new prime minister, to expedite efforts to resolve the issue.
He said maintaining good relations with neighbouring countries was crucial to ensuring smooth cooperation, particularly in addressing cross-border issues and promoting peace.
"I have had discussions twice with Thailand, including with its new prime minister, to expedite the matter.
"This is why we need to maintain good relations with our neighbours to ensure that cooperation can proceed smoothly," he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here today.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
Anwar said the project involved addressing erosion, as well as widening and deepening the river to improve water flow and reduce flooding.
He said resolving the issue at the Sungai Golok estuary would require close cooperation between the Malaysian and Thai governments.
"I hope we can finalise the matter within a month to reduce the impact of floods in Kelantan and southern Thailand," he said.
He also expressed appreciation to the Kelantan government, particularly the state secretary, for expediting the land acquisition process to facilitate the project.
Anwar said he hoped the initiative would usher in a new chapter of development for Rantau Panjang, which had been affected by recurring floods.
He said he would hold further discussions with the Thai government within the next month to ensure progress.
The prime minister was on a one-day working visit to Kelantan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PWD assistance gets largest share of Women's Ministry's 2027 budget
Article:
KUCHING: Assistance for people with disabilities (PWD) has received the largest allocation under the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry's 2027 Budget.
Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said RM1.5 billion of the RM3.3 billion allocated to the ministry would go towards assistance for PWD, benefiting more than 300,000 recipients.
"Among the improvements introduced is an increase in the allowance for bedridden PWD and chronically ill patients from RM500 to RM600 a month.
"Eligibility for the Disabled Workers' Allowance has also been expanded to individuals earning up to RM2,000 to ensure more people benefit from government assistance," she said in her speech at the ministry's Santun Kasih 2026 event here today.
Nancy said Budget 2027 provided an important direction for strengthening welfare, social protection and the empowerment of the people, particularly the ministry's target groups.
She said the government had also allocated RM1.3 billion for elderly assistance and the care sector, which was expected to benefit nearly 200,000 recipients.
"Besides financial assistance, the government plans to establish two National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) in Sarawak and Penang to strengthen facilities and care services for senior citizens.
"The service tax rate for elderly care services will also be reduced from eight to six per cent effective Jan 1, 2027," she said.
Assistance for children would also be increased to RM250 a month for those aged six and below, and RM200 a month for those aged between seven and 18.
She said the move was aimed at strengthening support for families in meeting basic needs while safeguarding children's development.
Nancy said women's empowerment would also be prioritised through the RM200 million Geran Sejahtera Madani grant, targeting 40,000 recipients, particularly to help them obtain equipment and training to generate income.
"Other measures include expanding tax relief for postnatal care services and improving maternity leave facilities for civil servants to support mothers' well-being," she said.
The Fertility Treatment Assistance and Infertility Advocacy Programme (BuAi) would also be expanded to benefit 2,000 couples, alongside the expansion of men's wellness services by the National Population and Family Development Board.
"All these initiatives complement the country's care economy agenda and strengthen the implementation of the Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan 2026-2030.
"The ministry is committed to ensuring every allocation benefits the people, while expanding access to quality and affordable care services, strengthening support for families and creating economic and employment opportunities in the sector," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says helping underprivileged will not impoverish country
Article:
KOTA BARU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said helping the underprivileged would not impoverish the country, but misconduct and poor governance could weaken and destroy it.
He said the government remained committed to assisting the poor and vulnerable while maintaining sound financial management.
This was reflected in the decision to raise civil servants' salaries, despite the move carrying an estimated cost of RM18 billion in 2026.
Anwar said cost-of-living assistance allocated this year amounted to RM16 billion, but the commitments would not burden the country.
He was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here today.
Anwar is on a one-day tour of Kelantan, with programmes focused on meeting the people.
He said the government would continue prioritising assistance for the lowest-income groups, particularly those in the B40 category, as outlined in Budget 2027.
The government was also focused on empowering small entrepreneurs, particularly women, through various assistance programmes.
In Kelantan, the Sejati Madani programme for entrepreneurs had received about 4,000 applications, of which 440 had been approved.
Anwar said the government would continue approving the remaining applications, noting that most applicants were women.
He said assistance programmes in Kelantan would place greater emphasis on empowering women, citing their track record in managing small businesses and repaying financing.
Drawing on his experience with Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, he said about 99 per cent of its female borrowers made repayments, while male borrowers tended to take slightly longer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah dies at 50
Article:
KANGAR: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad has died. She was 50.
Perlis Pas information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim confirmed her death in a social media post.
He said Wan Badariah died at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital at 4.26pm.
In May 2024, it was reported that she had been treated for complications from a thyroid condition.
She later recovered and resumed her duties.
Under the previous state administration, Wan Badariah served as state tourism committee chairman.
A lawyer by profession, she was Perlis Pas' first female candidate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pregnant mother hides behind counter as sword-wielding robber strikes jewellery shop
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A pregnant mother of three hid behind a counter in fear as a sword-wielding robber struck a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai yesterday.
Yani, who is in her 40s and three months pregnant, was working at the dessert shop next door when she heard a commotion.
"I heard a commotion and immediately hid behind the counter because I was frightened and did not know what was happening.
"It was only after the man had left that I heard the jewellery shop workers screaming 'robber, robber,' she said when met at the scene today.
Yani, who has worked at the dessert shop for just two months, said she never expected such an incident to happen there.
She eventually gathered enough courage to look outside and caught a glimpse of the suspect leaving the scene.
"He was wearing a long black raincoat, black pants and a helmet.
"What surprised me was that he was not running. He was just walking away," she said.
Yani said it all happened within minutes.
She said she later spoke to workers at the jewellery shop and learnt that the robber had been armed with a sharp object resembling a samurai sword, measuring between two and three feet long.
"The workers told me he had dropped the weapon inside the shop before leaving.
"However, he was still waving what appeared to be the sword's sheath as he walked away," she said.
Yani believed the suspect targeted the jewellery shop because security was inadequate.
"There was no security guard on duty at the shop. Perhaps that was why he chose this particular outlet.
"I also believe he deliberately chose to strike during Friday prayers because there would be fewer people around at that time," she said.
Meanwhile, supermarket employee Lim, 51, said he saw the suspect leaving while he was collecting shopping trolleys.
He said the man was fully covered and wore a face mask and helmet, making it difficult to identify him.
"I saw the man leave, but I could not see his face because it was completely covered.
"I could not intervene because I recently suffered a stroke. I was also worried that he might harm me," he said.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said investigators had recorded statements from employees of the jewellery shop and several other witnesses to assist in the investigation.
"Efforts are also underway to analyse closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to determine the
suspect's escape route
after leaving the premises," he said.
Police are continuing efforts to track down the suspect.
It was reported that the suspect fled with over RM300,000 in jewellery.
"An investigation paper has been opened under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code, while efforts are underway to track down the suspect," he said.
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters at 03-7966 2222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says technology must go hand in hand with good values
Article:
KOTA BARU: Parents must instil good values and moral character in their children as the country advances in technology and artificial intelligence.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would continue educating and reminding parents of their responsibility, stressing that national development must also be rooted in religious values, good manners and moral principles.
Anwar is in Kelantan for a one-day visit centred on meeting the people.
Speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan, Anwar said the issue was close to his heart and should not be viewed through a political lens.
"This is not about politics. It requires awareness and commitment from everyone.
"I am not trying to shirk my responsibilities as a member of the government. I will continue to do my best," he said.
Anwar said that while much attention was being given to entrepreneurship and economic development, equal emphasis must be placed on nurturing good character and moral values among the younger generation.
He stressed that parents played a crucial role in giving their children a strong foundation in life, particularly through religious education and good upbringing.
"We keep talking about entrepreneurs, but we must also talk about religion, manners and moral values.
"I will continue explaining this every day. Today, I am in Kelantan, and tomorrow I will be in another state.
"I will never grow tired of reminding parents about the basic things they must teach their children, including reading the Quran, practising good manners and developing strong moral values," he said.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah MMA seeks urgent deployment of doctors
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called on the Health Ministry to deploy more doctors from Peninsular Malaysia to critically understaffed healthcare facilities across Sabah.
Sabah MMA chairman Dr Brandon Patrick Senagang said reports by CodeBlue highlighted the severe workload and inadequate rest faced by doctors in Ranau, some of whom had worked between 48 and 72 consecutive hours.
"Their dedication deserves recognition, but it must be matched with practical support and timely relief. We cannot allow extraordinary personal sacrifice to become the routine basis on which essential healthcare services operate," he said in a statement.
He said 11 of Hospital Ranau's 19 medical officers had been transferred out following the recent permanent appointment exercise.
Of the seven designated replacements from outside Sabah, only one had reported for duty, leaving the hospital operating with nine doctors, including its director.
The Sabah State Health Department also reported an estimated statewide shortfall of 245 medical officers following the exercise, with 67 per cent of replacement candidates from outside Sabah failing to report for duty.
Brandon said the state health department's efforts to deploy three additional medical officers to Ranau in stages were constrained by similar shortages at other facilities across Sabah.
MMA Sabah called for an immediate, coordinated deployment programme from Peninsular Malaysia, with clear rotation periods, funded travel and accommodation, and adequate operational support.
"An immediate staffing response must run alongside the permanent recruitment exercise," he said.
The association welcomed a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent medical officer vacancies across Sabah and Sarawak, but said the proposed reporting date of Feb 15, 2027, was too far away to address immediate shortages.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NSTP attracts visitors with subscription promotions, exclusive merchandise
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The New Straits Times Press (NSTP) attracted visitors with print and e-paper subscription promotions at the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation's Health Screening Programme for Journalists here today.
Visitors were also offered exclusive merchandise as part of the promotions.
The promotional booth was set up in conjunction with the Malaysian Media Council's (MMC) second annual general meeting (AGM).
Visitors were introduced to NSTP's publications and subscription packages, including a complimentary one-year e-paper subscription promotion.
The booth also featured New Straits Times-branded merchandise, including T-shirts, tote bags and umbrellas, as part of efforts to engage readers and promote the company's publications.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil visited the booth and was welcomed by Media Prima News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim, who is also New Straits Times group editor.
NSTP branding and intellectual property executive Muhammad Hazeeq Abdul Wahid said the booth had received encouraging interest from visitors keen to learn more about the company's print and digital offerings.
"We have welcomed many visitors to our booth, and it is encouraging to see their interest in our print and digital publications.
"Many are excited to learn about the complimentary one-year e-paper subscription and the convenience of accessing news digitally.
"We are also introducing visitors to our NST merchandise, including T-shirts, tote bags and umbrellas, as part of our efforts to engage more closely with readers," he said.
Hazeeq said the promotional activities provided an opportunity for NSTP to connect with existing subscribers while introducing its publications to potential new readers.
He said the booth also allowed visitors to learn more about the benefits of digital subscriptions, particularly the convenience of accessing news through electronic editions.
The initiative reflects NSTP's continued efforts to strengthen reader engagement and promote its print and digital platforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen held for throwing stone at KTMB train
Article:
ARAU: A 14-year-old boy was detained after throwing a stone at a Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) train, shattering a carriage window and injuring a passenger.
The incident occurred on Thursday at 5.58pm as the
train was travelling
from Arau to Kodiang.
Arau police chief Superintendent Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said the teenager was detained at a house in Kampung Guar Sanji today.
"The boy admitted deliberately throwing a stone at the train window.
"He was with four friends near the Kampung Jelempok motorcycle overpass at the time," he said in a statement.
Mohsin said the four friends witnessed the incident but were not involved.
A window on the left side of the middle carriage was shattered.
A female passenger sustained minor injuries to her hand, while the train was delayed by 23 minutes.
Police seized a mobile phone, a SIM card and a stone to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief, which carries a penalty of between one and five years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan, Fadhlina confident economic strength, political stability will give PH an edge
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is confident that the country's improving economic conditions and current political stability could give the coalition an advantage in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Madani government's achievements over nearly four years in power, including the strengthening of the ringgit and inflow of foreign investments, must be effectively communicated to the people throughout the campaign period.
Speaking to the media at the Machap Jaya Nomination Centre at the JAPERUN Machap Jaya Complex in Bukit Bulat today, he said the election outcome remained open and would depend on the people's acceptance of the respective coalitions' proposals and efforts.
Ramanan, who is also human resources minister, said PH candidates needed to meet voters on the ground and explain the government's achievements, initiatives and plans for implementation in their interests.
"The information we have, our achievements and what we have implemented must reach the people. Otherwise, they will not know what is being done.
"Therefore, the delivery of messages and information to the people at the grassroots level needs to be improved," he said.
Meanwhile, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said PH's candidate for Machap Jaya, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin of PKR, had extensive political experience and was no stranger to voters in Melaka.
She said Lim's experience, having previously won the seat and served as Melaka's Women, Family Development, Welfare and Orang Asli Affairs executive councillor, gave her an advantage in terms of experience and familiarity among the local community.
Fadhlina said Machap Jaya was among the seats with significant potential for PH to win, although it was expected to face a stiff challenge from incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem (BN-MCA).
"I think this is an evenly matched contest, as both sides are relying on their respective track records, achievements and administrative service. This is a very good opportunity for PH, given the current situation which offers several advantages, including economic stability and the budget," said Fadhlina, who is also education minister.
She also commended PKR's decision to field three women candidates in this Melaka state election.
Earlier, Ramanan and Fadhlina, together with PKR vice-president performing the duties of deputy president and PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, who is also home minister, and PKR Central Leadership Council member Dr Maszlee Malik, accompanied Lim to the Machap Jaya nomination centre.
The Machap Jaya State seat will see a three-cornered contest involving Lim, Ngwe and B. Prasanth Kumar, who is representing Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will be held on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Employee transfers RM486,000 company money, deceived by individual impersonating employer
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A woman fell victim to a scam after being deceived by a person who impersonated her employer, resulting in the transfer of RM486,000 from the company.
Acting Johor Baru Utara district police chief superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said the 35-year-old victim was deceived through a short message service (SMS) from the individual who impersonated her company manager in the incident at 10am.
He said the victim was instructed to transfer the company's money to the suspect's account under the pretext of payment of a new contract.
Azrol Anuar said the victim, however, realised she was being scammed after being asked to make an additional transaction of the same amount under a different pretext.
"The victim also failed to contact the real employer through a WhatsApp call before discovering that the employer's phone number had been hacked," he said in a statement.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The public is advised to always be vigilant against any money transfer instructions and to check through the SemakMule portal or contact the NSRC 997 line if they fall victims to scams.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AGC reviewing candidate selection for proposed separation of top legal roles
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) is reviewing provisions on the selection of candidates under a proposal to separate the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this followed the tabling of the Bill on the proposed separation.
"The Bill on the proposed separation of the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor has been tabled and has gone through the proper process, including consideration by the Parliamentary Special Select Committee (PSSC).
"On the issue of candidates, we are reviewing a provision concerning how they should be selected," he said.
He was speaking at the opening and handover of recreational facilities under the Attorney-General's Chambers' Kampung Angkat Madani programme in Kampung Kok Lanas yesterday.
Reports previously stated the PSSC would resume its meeting after receiving feedback from the A-GC on the proposed separation of the roles.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the A-GC had been given two weeks to provide a detailed response.
On Mar 3, the Constitution (Amendment) Bill (No. 2) 2026, which seeks to separate the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor, was referred to the PSSC.
Under the proposed framework, the public prosecutor would oversee all criminal prosecutions, while the attorney-general would serve as the government's legal adviser on matters other than criminal law.
The public prosecutor would be appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong at His Majesty's discretion, on the advice of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission, after consulting the Conference of Rulers.
The proposal differs from the current arrangement, under which the
attorney-general is appointed
by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Meanwhile, Dusuki said RM500,000 had been allocated to upgrade public facilities and improve residents' well-being under the Attorney-General's Chambers' Kampung Angkat Madani programme in Kampung Kok Lanas.
He said the infrastructure improvements covered not only physical facilities but also supported healthy lifestyles, small-scale economic activities and the well-being of the local community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police tracking down suspects in shooting incident in Sitiawan
Article:
IPOH: Police are tracking down suspects involved in a shooting incident in which several shots were fired at a BMW in front of a house in Taman Hijau, Kampung Koh, near Sitiawan, yesterday.
Manjung police chief assistant commissioner Hasbullah Abd Rahman said that police received a report from a man at 1.54pm yesterday regarding the incident.
He said the incident was believed to have occurred at 4.16am, when the complainant heard what sounded like gunshots while inside his house.
The complainant later discovered about 9am that there were four bullet marks on the right-side door of his vehicle.
"A review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at the scene showed two unidentified suspects approaching the vehicle on a motorcycle.
"One of the suspects then fired shots at the vehicle before fleeing. Police have opened an investigation paper and the case is being investigated under Section 39 of the Arms Act 1960," he said in a statement, adding that efforts to track down the suspects were ongoing.
Those with any information can contact the Manjung district police headquarters or its Operations Room at 05-688 6222, the WhatsApp hotline at 017-682 8005, or any nearby police station.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, Hasbullah said police had arrested a man and two women, aged between 24 and 26, on suspicion of being involved in the theft of a Toyota Hilux belonging to a man in Taman Mas 2, Sitiawan.
He said the three suspects had been remanded for six days, from Oct 28 to Nov 2, to facilitate investigations under Section 379A of the Penal Code.
"About 5.30pm on Oct 27, a team of policemen from the Manjung district police headquarters arrested all three suspects, who were believed to be involved in the incident.
"Police also seized a car key reader device believed to have been used in the vehicle thefts, as well as several other items.
"Interrogations found that the suspects admitted to being involved in eight vehicle theft cases, four in Perak and four in Kuala Lumpur, using the same modus operandi and targeting four-wheel-drive vehicles," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Waze ban: PSD confident of full compliance among civil servants
Article:
KAMPAR: The Public Service Department (PSD) is confident that civil servants will fully comply with the ban on the use of the Waze navigation application.
Public Service director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the compliance rate among civil servants had yet to be determined, as the government had only recently announced the directive.
Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that civil servants would take the matter seriously and comply with the ban, which was imposed for security reasons.
"Civil servants are no longer allowed to use Waze due to security concerns. We have also learned from what happened to other countries that used the application, he said after officiating at the closing ceremony of the 'Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani JPA' programme at SK Kota Baharu today.
On Oct 21, the government decided to
ban all civil servants
from using the Waze navigation application to protect government information and users' personal data from  the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the decision took into account the fact that Waze Mobile Ltd, which controls user data, is incorporated and operates under Israeli law.
Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Dahlan said RM1.465 million had been allocated to improve infrastructure, upgrade public facilities and support educational programmes under the Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani programme for residents of Kampung Kota Bharu and students of SMK Malim Nawar.
He said RM500,000 from the Finance Ministry and an additional RM35,000 from PSD were set aside for eight physical projects under the Kampung Angkat Madani initiative, including upgrades to the mosque, community hall, health clinic, police station and pavilion at SK Kota Baharu, as well as the construction of a village landmark and the provision of smart boards.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also said collaboration with the Rural and Regional Development Ministry had resulted in the installation of 40 solar-powered streetlights worth RM380,000, while the Implementation Coordination Unit under the Prime Minister's Department had allocated RM450,000 for the construction of a new multipurpose hall with two badminton courts.
He said an allocation of RM90,000 was also provided to SMK Malim Nawar to upgrade its computer laboratory, Design and Technology (RBT) workshop and science laboratories, with another RM10,000 earmarked for educational development programmes for students and teachers.
"Various community and educational activities have also been held, including a korban programme, GP Joran fishing competition, traditional games, health and psychological outreach programme, Tuisyen Madani, gotong-royong activities and Wira Komuniti Carnival," he said.
The closing ceremony also saw 97 families in Kampung Kota Bharu receive Bakul Rahmah aid, while schools received contributions and department's strategic partners were recognised for their support.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also praised the school team for winning a gold medal for its Ecowire Roll innovation at the International Innovation and Entrepreneurship Expo 2026 on Oct 25.
He also highlighted the achievement of a female student from SMK Malim Nawar who was selected to represent Selangor in football.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said these achievements showed that children from rural areas could excel when given the right opportunities, facilities and support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 17 detained over brawl in Ampang Jaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested 17 people to assist in investigations into a brawl at the Lembah Jaya Flats in Ampang Jaya early today.
Ampang Jaya police chief ACP assistant commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said police received a report about the incident at Jalan 3, Lembah Jaya Utara, at 2.07am.
He said policemen sent to the scene found no ongoing brawl, but a group of people and detained the 17 people.
"They have been remanded for between two and three days, with the case being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code," he said in a statement today.
Those with information can contact the police to assist in the investigation.
Earlier, two videos showing a group of people gathered in the car park of the flats went viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fire damages house, EV in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: A single-storey house and an electric vehicle (EV) parked on its porch were damaged in a fire at Taman Kempadang Sejahtera here today.
No casualties were reported in the 9am incident.
A Pahang Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said 15 firefighters from the Kuantan and Indera Mahkota fire stations arrived at the scene at 9.29am.
The fire destroyed about 75 per cent of the house, mainly the living room and kitchen.
An EV parked in the porch was also partially damaged.
"The department's Forensic Unit was deployed to the scene. The cause of the fire is still under investigation," said the statement.
Earlier, several images showing flames engulfing the house and the vehicle went viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man with drug-related records arrested with 791 yaba pills
Article:
KOTA BARU: A 47-year-old man, with four drug-related records, and found with 791 yaba pills weighing 87.71g, was arrested in a raid at Kampung Pasir Parit, Chetok in Pasir Mas last night.
Pasir Mas police chief assistant commissioner Mazlan Hassan said the raid was conducted by a team from the Tok Uban police station, who also seized methamphetamine (syabu) drugs.
Initial investigation found that the suspect had four previous drug offences and the suspect tested positive for methamphetamine, he said in a Facebook page.
The case is being investigated under Sectio 39B and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Express train derails after hitting bear in Hokkaido, services cancelled
Article:
HOKKAIDO: A train bound for the northern Hokkaido city of Wakkanai derailed after hitting a bear late Friday, though none of the crew or 32 passengers were hurt, its operator said, Kyodo News reported.
The first car of the four-car Sarobetsu limited express train derailed after the collision around 10.50 pm between Teshio-Nakagawa and Toikambetsu stations, according to JR Hokkaido.
The company has cancelled all services on the 130-kilometre section between Wakkanai and Otoineppu on Saturday.
The passengers on the train were transported by taxis from the site of the collision. – BERNAMA-KYODO
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shooting at California Halloween store kills one, wounds six
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: A shooting at a Halloween store in northern California killed one person and wounded six on Friday, police said, adding investigators had not yet identified who was responsible.
The incident occurred shortly before 8.30pm (0330 GMT Saturday) at a Spirit Halloween store at a shopping mall in Fairfield, about 47 miles (76 kilometres) northeast of San Francisco.
Fairfield police chief Dan Marshall told reporters one person was killed and six others were hospitalised with gunshot wounds. At least three were in critical condition, he added.
"There is still a very active crime scene and investigation going on right now," Marshall said late Friday, noting police had not yet identified the "suspect or suspects" responsible.
The shooting took place hours before the start of Halloween, which is celebrated in the United States on Saturday.
Marshall said no areas outside of the Solano Town Centre mall were on lockdown.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tenaganita raises concerns over handcuffing of Myanmar boys
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaganita has called for an investigation into the reported handcuffing of three Myanmar children charged with criminal intimidation, citing concerns over their treatment and rights.
The rights group said the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia's (Suhakam) Office of the Children's Commissioner should intervene to ensure the children receive appropriate legal and psychosocial support.
Its executive director, Glorene Das, said authorities must uphold the Child Act 2001 and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, regardless of a child's nationality or immigration status.
"We recognise that allegations of wrongdoing must be investigated and that victims deserve justice, but justice for one person must never come at the expense of the fundamental rights and dignity of children," she said in a statement.
She said the reported use of restraints, their initial detention and concerns over language interpretation raised questions about whether proper safeguards had been observed.
"While we welcome the High Court's subsequent decision to grant bail, it does not erase the fear, humiliation and trauma these children may have experienced," she said.
The three, comprising two 11-year-olds and a 12-year-old, pleaded not guilty at the Bukit Mertajam magistrate's court to jointly
threatening an elderly woman
with several objects, including a mop, iron rod, fluorescent light tube and stones.
They were charged under Section 506 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code. If convicted, they face up to two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MHA top brass must answer for inaccurate information on TuJu, says Fahmi
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Highway Authority's (MHA) top brass must be held accountable if inaccurate information was provided concerning the TuJu navigation application, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said senior management must take responsibility for any inaccurate advice or information presented during official discussions.
"If inaccurate information was presented, the senior management of the organisation concerned must be held accountable.
"They must be made to account for whatever advice or information that they have given," he told reporters after officiating the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation's Health Screening Programme for Journalists here today.
Fahmi was responding to questions about the controversy surrounding TuJu and the Waze navigation application.
MHA chairperson Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad previously clarified that the TuJu navigation application was developed primarily to improve services along tolled highways, rather than to compete directly with Waze.
His explanation comes amid questions over the government's promotion of TuJu as an alternative to Waze, following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for Malaysians to switch to the locally developed application over national security concerns.
Asked whether the government would advise MHA on TuJu's functions, Fahmi said he had not attended the meeting in question and was unaware of what had been discussed.
"I did not attend that meeting. I do not have information about what was discussed," he said.
Earlier, the government announced the ban on Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
The Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's status as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
Waze has denied allegations that it collects sensitive government information or allows third parties to exploit users' personal data.
The company maintained that it operates under strict privacy policies and complies with applicable data protection standards.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ang's hard work earns him prestigious UMPSA Royal Education Award
Article:
PEKAN: Raised in a modest family, with his father working as a van driver, Ang Cheng Long never imagined receiving one of Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah's (UMPSA) highest academic honours.
The 24-year-old, who graduated with a Bachelor of Chemical Engineering with Honours, was surprised when he was named recipient of the prestigious Royal Education Award at the university's 21st Convocation Ceremony today.
Ang said he had never considered himself the most deserving candidate, believing other students had performed better academically.
"The recognition means a lot to me and my family, whose unwavering support has been instrumental throughout my university journey.
"Honestly, I was surprised when my name was announced as the recipient of this prestigious award. I am grateful to UMPSA for placing its trust in me," he said when met.
Meanwhile, Shakirah Izzati Muhammad Firdaus, who graduated with a Bachelor of Computer Science (Cyber Security) with Honours from the Faculty of Computing, said her main focus had always been doing well in her semester examinations, making the award an unexpected bonus.
[[nid:1567628]]
"I never set out to win this award, so being named a recipient and having the opportunity to receive it on stage is a tremendous honour.
"For me, this achievement is not just about receiving an award, but also about giving back to my family and contributing to society in the future," said the youngest of four siblings.
The two were among 150 graduates who received academic excellence awards and prizes in recognition of their achievements in academics, leadership, innovation and professional development.
UMPSA vice-chancellor Professor Dr Yatimah Alias said 3,345 graduates would receive their scrolls during the university's four-day convocation ceremony, which began today.
She said the graduates comprised PhD recipients, master's degree holders, bachelor's degree graduates, dual-degree recipients, diploma holders and graduates from UMPSA Advanced's lifelong learning programmes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi proposes annual health screenings for journalists
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil wants more than 12,000 accredited journalists nationwide to undergo health screenings at least once a year.
He said the proposal would be discussed with the Malaysian Media Council (MMM) and media organisations to determine how healthcare could be made more accessible to media practitioners.
"We want to encourage all media practitioners to undergo health screening at least once a year," he said at a press conference after officiating the CVSKL Foundation's Health Screening Programme for Journalists here today.
Fahmi said the Information Department could ask journalists whether they had undergone medical screenings when applying for annual media accreditation cards.
However, when asked whether screenings could become a condition for obtaining the cards, he said no such requirement had been discussed.
"For now, it is merely a suggestion," he said.
Fahmi said the government would also need to consider journalists working outside the Klang Valley, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, who might face difficulties accessing medical facilities.
He said early detection was important to prevent complications from conditions including diabetes and cardiovascular conditions.
The minister recalled receiving an urgent call from a journalist he knew who needed heart surgery after doctors discovered a blockage.
He said the incident highlighted the importance of regular medical examinations despite journalists' demanding schedules.
[[nid:1567622]]
"We must make time for our health before something happens," he said.
Fahmi said members of parliament were required to undergo annual health screenings and submit their medical records to Parliament.
He hoped a similar culture of preventive healthcare could be encouraged among journalists without making screenings compulsory.
Fahmi also thanked the CVSKL Foundation for working with the Malaysian Media Council to support health screenings for media workers.
He pledged to work with both organisations to mobilise additional funding ahead of National Journalists' Day in 2027.
The initiative, he said, should reach as many as possible of the more than 12,000 journalists holding media accreditation cards.
The Malaysian Media Council's annual general meeting has been postponed until tomorrow due to a lack of quorum.
The meeting, which was scheduled to discuss the council's affairs, including a proposed RM4.58 million expenditure allocation for 2027, could not proceed formally and was instead converted into a briefing for members present.
Under the Malaysian Media Council Act, the quorum for an AGM is one-third of the council's total membership.
Among those present were MMM board members, including Media Prima News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim, who is also New Straits Times group editor; Star Media Group chief content officer Datin Esther Ng; and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin.
Earlier, MMM chair Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan outlined the council's priorities for 2027, including strengthening public trust in journalism, ensuring media sustainability and improving governance.
She also highlighted ongoing efforts to develop a code of conduct and ethics framework, alongside plans to expand training and awareness programmes for media practitioners.
The council is examining possible reforms to longstanding legislation affecting the media, including the Printing Presses and Publications Act, Sedition Act and Official Secrets Act.
Nallini also raised concerns about the sustainability of vernacular newspapers and the need for fairer competition between traditional media organisations and major digital platforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt seeks Google, TikTok partnerships to boost media revenue
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government is looking to expand cooperation with technology platforms, including Google and TikTok, to help Malaysian media organisations develop new revenue streams amid declining advertising income.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry was exploring initiatives such as Project Sigma 2.0 with Google, alongside opportunities involving the Malaysian Media Council, Content Forum and TikTok.
He said the efforts were aimed at helping media companies reduce their dependence on traditional advertising, which had increasingly shifted to social media platforms.
"We also intend to pursue several initiatives, such as Project Sigma 2.0 with Google, and leverage relationships through the Malaysian Media Council and Content Forum with platforms such as TikTok to help our media colleagues find new sources of revenue," he said at a press conference after officiating the CVSKL Foundation's Health Screening Programme for Journalists today.
He said the changing advertising landscape had placed considerable pressure on news organisations, contributing to financial and operational challenges across the industry.
In his earlier speech, Fahmi criticised some major technology platforms for failing to cooperate adequately with efforts to support traditional media.
He said certain companies were using their connections with the White House to avoid providing sufficient cooperation, although he did not identify the platforms concerned.
He said the government was pursuing several approaches to help media organisations remain viable, including financial assistance through the Media Innovation Fund.
A further RM30 million has been allocated under the fund's second phase, with applications opening on Nov 1 and closing on Nov 14.
The initiative covers five areas, including personnel training, software and technology adoption, equipment procurement, content research and development, and subscriptions to news services and media content.
Fahmi said media companies were free to choose technologies and vendors suited to their operations, including artificial intelligence tools.
However, he said that technological transformation should help news organisations become more productive rather than lead to indiscriminate staff retrenchments.
He also encouraged companies facing financial difficulties to approach the ministry for assistance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CSA does not signal PH-Bersatu electoral cooperation, says Fahmi
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu have not held discussions on a broader electoral pact following the signing of the
confidence and supply agreement
(CSA) by 13 opposition MPs.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the agreement was limited to the current parliamentary term and did not extend to future electoral cooperation.
"There have been no discussions on that," he said when asked whether the CSA could pave the way for a broader electoral pact between PH and Bersatu.
Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said any member of parliament interested in signing the agreement was welcome to do so.
"For now, any MP who wishes to sign the memorandum of understanding or CSA may do so.
"There is no requirement to provide any support in the future. It is for the current parliamentary term, and there have been no further discussions beyond that," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after officiating the CVSKL Foundation's Health Screening Programme for Journalists today.
Asked whether PH and Bersatu were considering a broader electoral arrangement, Fahmi said no such discussions had taken place within PH or PKR.
"For now, Pakatan Harapan and Keadilan in particular have not discussed that.
"We are focused on the Melaka election and will take it one step at a time," he said.
His remarks follow the signing of the CSA by 13 opposition MPs, which the government has described as a positive development for political stability.
The agreement has raised questions about whether parliamentary cooperation could eventually lead to electoral collaboration between PH and Bersatu.
The agreement involved six Bersatu MPs, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and six independent MPs who had previously declared support for Anwar.
The six Bersatu MPs were Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin (Pagoh), Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Datuk Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
The six independent MPs were Datuk Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Tanjong Karang), Datuk Syed Abu Hussin Hafiz Syed Abdul Fasal (Bukit Gantang), Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar), Mohd Azizi Abu Naim (Gua Musang), Zahari Kechik (Jeli) and Datuk Dr Suhaili Abdul Rahman (Labuan).
The possibility of wider cooperation has attracted attention ahead of the Nov 14 Melaka election, where both sides have announced candidates in several overlapping constituencies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men held with 540 packets of ketum juice in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: Two men were arrested on suspicion of processing ketum juice at a house in Jaya Gading here yesterday.
The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 540 packets of ketum juice and three sacks containing ketum leaves during a raid at 2pm.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid was conducted under Op Taring Mitra after a team monitored the premises.
"The team spotted a Proton Saga entering the house before moving in to conduct checks when two men got out of the vehicle.
"Checks led to the discovery of 540 packets of ketum juice and three sacks containing about 33kg of ketum leaves, with an estimated total value of RM17,520," he said in a statement today.
He said the team also seized several kitchen appliances, including a gas cylinder and pots believed to have been used to boil the ketum leaves.
"Investigations revealed that both suspects obtained ketum leaves from outside Pahang and used the house to process the juice before selling it," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952, which provides for a maximum fine of RM100,000, jail of up to five years, or both, upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Rais to announce special pledges for Sungai Udang voters
Article:
SUNGAI UDANG: Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the Sungai Udang state seat Datuk Rais Yasin will unveil a special pledge for the constituency after the coalition announces its election manifesto.
He said the pledge would address the specific needs of Sungai Udang residents.
"Let us wait for the state BN manifesto first. After that, I will have a specific pledge for the people of Sungai Udang, so stay tuned," he told reporters at the BN Sungai Udang main operations room in Bandar Baru Sungai Udang.
Earlier, during the nomination process at the Rela Training Academy's multipurpose hall in Sungai Udang, he was accompanied by senior Umno and Pas leaders, including Umno vice-president and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad; Umno Supreme Council member and Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah; and Pas Central Working Committee member Senator Nik Mohamad Abduh Nik Abdul Aziz.
The former state executive councillor for housing, local government, drainage, climate change and disaster management is facing a three-cornered contest against Major (Rtd) Abdullah Mahadi of Bersatu and Mohd Ridzuan Abdul Rahman of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
In the 2021 Melaka state election, the Sungai Udang seat was won by Perikatan Nasional candidate Dr Mohd Aleef Yusof, who secured 6,789 votes with a majority of 530.
He defeated BN candidate Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad, who received 6,259 votes, Pakatan Harapan candidate Hasmorni Tamby with 2,035 votes, and independent candidate Mohd Zahar Hashim with 471 votes.
Following the election, BN formed the state government, winning 21 of the 28 state seats, while PH secured five and PN won two.
The campaign period for the 16th Melaka state election will run for 14 days, beginning today. Early voting is scheduled for Nov 10, while polling day is set for Nov 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chickens dead before slaughter do not meet halal requirements, says Jakim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chickens found to have died before slaughter do not meet halal requirements, the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) said, following a raid on an abattoir in Puchong, Selangor.
Jakim director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee said if the claims were confirmed, the chickens would not meet the requirements for halal slaughter.
"Under Islamic law, animals that are permissible for consumption must be slaughtered in accordance with the conditions stipulated by syarak.
"One of these conditions is that the chickens must still be alive when slaughtered. In other words, if the chickens had died before slaughter, they would be considered carrion," he said when contacted today.
It was reported that more than
6.5 tonnes of raw chicken
suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughter requirements and halal certification standards had been seized in a raid on a warehouse in Puchong two days ago.
Sirajuddin said the department viewed the matter seriously as it involved compliance with Islamic law, hygiene and public confidence in the halal status of chicken supplies in the market.
"Based on initial inspections, the premises were suspected of carrying out the slaughter, processing and distribution of fresh chicken without permits or approval from the local authorities.
"Companies operating without valid permits or licences are not eligible to apply for the Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM), as one of the requirements for certification is to obtain a municipal council licence," he said.
On the distribution of chicken supplies from the abattoir, he said the premises were not holders of SPHM issued by Jakim.
"Therefore, any sales records from the premises are not included in Jakim's halal certification monitoring records. In this matter, the relevant authorities must act within their respective jurisdictions.
"Action to trace and recall chicken already in the market must take into account the provisions of existing laws.
"Relevant enforcement agencies can take action within their respective jurisdictions to stop sales, segregate stocks and carry out recalls or seize identified supplies," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police plan to expand collaboration with Media Prima through Karnival Jom Heboh
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police are exploring ways to expand their collaboration with Media Prima Bhd (MPB), including participating in future 'Karnival Jom Heboh' events to provide more services directly to the public.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the carnival was not merely an entertainment and sales event, but also an effective platform for police to engage with the public through dedicated service counters and safety awareness programmes.
"Our collaboration with MPB may not be limited to Karnival Jom Heboh. We hope to continue working together at other events wherever our services are needed.
"We see opportunities to expand this cooperation. For example, the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department could set up a counter to facilitate summons payments, making it easier for the public to settle outstanding fines," he said when met at the Jom Heboh Carnival Johor Baru 2026.
He said police participation in such events could also involve the Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department.
"The department can continuously raise public awareness about police duties while fostering cooperation between the community and police to ensure security remains at its best," he said.
Earlier, Khalid visited various booths at the carnival at Padang B of the shopping mall, including the Johor Police Families Association (Perkep) booth.
He said the event also provided an opportunity for Perkep, which has more than 80,000 members nationwide, to generate income.
"I see this as an opportunity for Perkep to venture into business. I believe the association will use this platform to gain a better understanding of how businesses operate while improving the economic well-being of its members and their families," he said.
Also present were Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad, Perkep chairman Puan Sri Dr Munirah Che Rose, MPB group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid and Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer Datuk Mohd Efendi Omar.
Meanwhile, Munirah said this was Perkep's third participation in Karnival Jom Heboh, following successful events in Miri and Kota Samarahan.
She said the association hoped to continue its collaboration with the carnival at its next venue, Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur.
The three-day Karnival 2026 runs until tomorrow, featuring various activities including sales booths, performances by local artistes, family activities and offers on a range of daily necessities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Election victory not about who shouts loudest, says Saifuddin
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan has pledged to conduct a peaceful campaign throughout the Melaka election, having learnt that electoral victory should not be determined by who shouts the loudest, but by who earns the people's trust.
Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said PH had drawn a firm line against the politics of hatred and division, with the aim of ensuring peaceful political competition without undermining racial harmony.
He said the coalition had outlined three key messages for its campaign namely respecting differences of opinion in a democracy, ensuring the contest remained free from slander and personal attacks, and offering solutions through its election manifesto.
"Our red line is that we completely reject the politics of hatred and division, as well as the belief that defending our own race requires us to oppress others, or that for our race to succeed, other communities must have no place.
"We reject this outright. This is our campaign principle and our red line," he said at a press conference at the PH Melaka main operations centre here today.
Also present were Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli and DAP representative Young Syefura Othman.
Saifuddin said the first message would be reflected in PH's commitment to peaceful campaigning, adding that electoral victory should not be determined by who shouted the loudest, but by who earned the people's trust.
He said the second message was aimed at ensuring the campaign did not become a platform for slander or personal attacks, allowing voters to assess the proposals put forward by each candidate.
"This is not a contest of slander, much less a competition over who can launch the strongest personal attacks.
"It is about choosing ideas, policies, track records, solutions to problems and the people's welfare," he said.
On the third message, Saifuddin said PH would elaborate on its proposals through its election manifesto, which would be launched soon.
He said the manifesto would include measures to create employment opportunities and address issues concerning the future of young people.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin said PH was fielding 24 candidates from its three component parties: 10 from PKR and seven each from DAP and Amanah.
He said the coalition was offering a combination of experienced candidates and new faces whom it believed could put forward meaningful proposals to voters in their respective constituencies.
Saifuddin said PH's campaign slogan, "Melaka Rumah Kita" (Melaka Our Home), reflected its vision of the state as a peaceful and harmonious place where people of different races, religions and cultures could live together.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No unhealthy readings: Cheras highest at 77 as 47 areas nationwide record moderate API readings this afternoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A total of 47 areas across the country recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at a moderate level as of this evening, while 21 areas recorded good air quality.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollution Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Cheras here recorded the highest moderate API reading at 77, followed by Batu Muda (72). In Selangor, the affected areas include Johan Setia (76), Klang (74), Shah Alam (64), Banting (62), Petaling Jaya (60), and Kuala Selangor (55).
In Johor, the areas are Larkin (73), Kluang (67), Tangkak (62), Pasir Gudang (61), Segamat (56), as well as Pengerang and Kota Tinggi (53 each).
Negeri Sembilan recorded moderate readings in Nilai (69), Seremban (63), and Port Dickson (57), while in Perak, the areas involved are Tasek Ipoh (66), Seri Manjung (56), Pegoh in Ipoh (55), and Taiping (54).
Putrajaya recorded a reading of 65, while in Penang, the areas are Seberang Perai (64), Seberang Jaya (55), and Minden (52).
In Sarawak, seven areas recorded moderate readings: Mukah (64), IPD Serian (59), Kuching (57), Samalaju (56), Sri Aman (55), Sibu (53), and Samarahan (51).
Melaka recorded readings in Bandaraya Melaka (63), Bukit Rambai (62), and Alor Gajah (61), while in Pahang, the area involved is Balok Baru in Kuantan (61).
In Sabah, the areas are Tawau (61), Keningau (55), Kimanis (54), and Sandakan (52), while in Kelantan, they involve Kota Bharu (59) and Tanah Merah (52).
Kedah also recorded moderate readings in Sungai Petani (58) and Kulim Hi-Tech (51), while Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu recorded a reading of 55, and Labuan recorded 52.
Meanwhile, a total of 21 areas recorded good API readings as of this evening, compared to 24 areas in the morning.
API readings between 0 and 50 are categorized as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Perlis PAS announces death of Mata Ayer rep Wan Badariah
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 31 — Mata Ayer assemblywoman Wan Badariah Wan Saad died at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) here at 4.26pm today.
Perlis PAS Information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim announced her death in a post on the Perlis PAS Facebook page.
He also extended condolences to her family and urged the public to pray for her soul.
“May Allah shower His blessings upon her soul, forgive her sins and place her among the faithful and the righteous.
“My condolences to all members of her family,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Baby buried in Kapit still hospitalised; mother’s postpartum depression link unconfirmed, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 31 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has yet to receive medical confirmation on whether the mother of a baby boy found buried in Kapit recently was suffering from postpartum depression.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registered counsellors and hospital medical personnel had important roles to play in identifying the underlying issues faced by the mother.
“We do not know yet, which is why counsellors play a very important role. The Health Ministry also needs to involve the doctors and nurses handling the case.
“I cannot comment beyond what we know so far, as the police are still investigating the case, but our protection team is working with the family and counsellors to determine the actual problem so that they can provide assistance,” she told a press conference after officiating the KPWKM Santuni Kasih Programme here today.
Nancy said discussions on whether the baby would be placed under the care of family members or other suitable parties had yet to be concluded, as both the mother and baby were understood to still be receiving hospital treatment.
She also advised mothers in need of emotional and postnatal health support to seek assistance through the MamaCare initiative, managed by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN).
Earlier, Kapit police chief DSP Rohana Nanu was reported as saying that a baby boy who was still alive was found buried in the ground near a rented house in Jalan Airport, Kapit, on Wednesday.
The baby, who was initially reported to be in critical condition, was rushed to Sibu Hospital for specialist treatment, while the case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Not compulsory, but journalists, your annual check-up could soon come with your press card
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 31 — The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) should explore mechanisms to encourage media practitioners to undergo health screenings during the process of issuing media passes.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed initiative is crucial to ensure that as many as possible of the 12,000 personnel in the media sector benefit and have health issues identified at an early stage.
“I do not want to say to make it compulsory, but we must encourage them. Perhaps the Information Department, before issuing the annual media accreditation card, could ask if they have undergone a medical check-up,” he said today.
He said this in his speech at the launch of the Journalists’ Health Screening Programme with the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation ahead of the 2026 MMC Annual General Meeting here.
Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, CVSKL Foundation chairman Tan Sri Rashpal Singh, ECM Libra Foundation chairman Datuk Seri Kalimullah Masheerul Hassan and MMC chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan.
Fahmi later told reporters that the proposal for media practitioners to undergo annual health screening has not been set as a prerequisite for media card holders, adding that it would be discussed with the MMC in detail first.
“We will discuss this with the Media Council (and) with all media companies to assess its feasibility; for instance, if this initiative involves facilities in the Klang Valley, it may pose some difficulties for our colleagues in Sabah and Sarawak, or in areas outside the Klang Valley.
“We do not intend to make it compulsory, but we would like to encourage all media teams to undergo health screenings at least once a year. That is our intention,” he said.
On today’s programme, he said the RM1 million initiative, contributed by ECM Libra Foundation to the CVSKL Foundation, aimed to help improve access to preventive healthcare services, particularly for active and former journalists.
“We view problems involving the health of journalists as one of the key issues. These screenings can help identify non-communicable diseases at an early stage, allowing us to provide assistance earlier and help prevent any untoward incidents from occurring,” he added. — Bernama

Title: ‘Boss’ texts, RM486,000 gone: Johor Bahru woman duped by fake employer
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 31 — A woman fell victim to a scam after being deceived by an individual who impersonated her employer, resulting in the transfer of RM486,000 from the company.
Acting Johor Bahru Utara district police chief Supt Azrol Anuar Nor said the 35-year-old victim was deceived through a short message service (SMS) from the individual who impersonated her company manager in the incident at 10 am.
He said the victim was instructed to transfer the company’s money to the suspect’s account under the pretext of payment of a new contract.
Azrol Anuar said the victim, however, realised she was being scammed after being asked to make an additional transaction of the same amount under a different pretext.
“The victim also failed to contact the real employer through a WhatsApp call before discovering that the employer’s phone number had been hacked,” he said in a statement.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The public is advised to always be vigilant against any money transfer instructions and to check through the SemakMule portal or contact the NSRC 997 line if they fall victims to scams. — Bernama
Editor’s note: Supt stands for Superintendent. SMS stands for Short Message Service. NSRC stands for National Scam Response Centre.

Title: Puchong chicken supplier shut for two weeks after halal breach discovery, restaurants told to stop buying from it
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — A premises in Puchong, suspected of slaughtering, processing and distributing chicken without valid halal certification, was found to be using the electric water-bath stunning method.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said preliminary inspections found that the electrical voltage used was believed to be too high, causing the chickens to die instantly before undergoing slaughter in accordance with Islamic law.
“Early this morning, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), in collaboration with the police, the Selangor Department of Environment (DOE), the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and the Petaling District Health Office, led a raid on premises allegedly involved in slaughtering chickens in a manner that did not comply with Islamic requirements.
“Preliminary investigations found that the premises used the stunning method, whereby the chickens were found dead before being slaughtered. This means they were essentially slaughtering carcasses rather than live chickens, as required under Islamic teachings,” he told reporters.
He said this after attending the 2026 Selangor-level Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah (ASWJ) Fundamental Declaration Programme, which was also attended by Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad, at the Dewan Syarahan dan Muzakarah Islam, Masjid Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah, here today.
He added that the situation had raised serious doubts over compliance with Islamic law, and the halal status of the processed chicken products, making this a key focus of the authorities’ investigation to determine the actual operating methods used.
Elaborating, Salehuddin said preliminary investigations also found that the slaughterhouse had been operating since 2004, and was believed to be owned by a Muslim, besides supplying processed chicken to restaurants also owned by Muslims.
“If it is true that this is a Muslim-owned factory which had killed the chickens before slaughtering them, this is a highly irresponsible act, and we will ensure that firm action is taken.
“The company has been operating for a long time, for more than 20 years. I am therefore rather perplexed as to how something like this could happen, and why they would so easily deceive Muslims when they themselves are Muslims.
Salehuddin said the issue was also linked to the absence of mandatory halal certification requirements for certain premises. However, operators should be aware that the meat supply in question was prohibited under Islamic law.
Following the raid, he said that the authorities had ordered the factory premises to be closed for two weeks under health regulations, to allow for a detailed assessment and investigation.
In this regard, Salehuddin urged restaurant owners receiving supplies from the company to stop using them immediately, and report any suspicious information to Jais, Jakim or the police.
“I urge Muslims, restaurant operators and food business owners to check the source of their chicken supplies, in particular, as they must ensure that the food they serve is suitable for consumption by Muslims.
“Earlier, Jais seized more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken, worth RM85,400, after finding that the poultry had been processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering requirements. The seizure was made during a raid at a warehouse in Puchong at 12.40 am today, under Op Taring Chiller.
Earlier, the 2026 Selangor-level ASWJ Fundamental Declaration programme brought together nearly 500 participants, including teachers, mosque administrators, marriage registrars, local authorities (PBT) and religious agencies, to deepen their understanding of the importance of safeguarding the faith, through presentations of two working papers. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Mais stands for Majlis Agama Islam Selangor, Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, and Jakim stands for Jabatan Kemajuan Islam Malaysia. PBT stands for Pihak Berkuasa Tempatan, and Op stands for Operasi. ASWJ stands for Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah, an Arabic term for mainstream Sunni Islam.

Title: No five- or six-cornered fights in 28 seats: Melaka’s 2026 ballot looks very different from 2021
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The 16th Melaka State Election features 11 straight fights and 11 three-cornered contests across the 28 state constituencies, following the conclusion of the nomination process today.
The remaining six constituencies will see four-cornered contests, marking a significant shift from the 2021 state election, which was dominated by five- and six-cornered races, with no straight fights.
Among the straight fights attracting attention is Tanjung Bidara, where incumbent Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh of Barisan Nasional (BN) faces Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who is making his electoral debut.
In Rim, incumbent Datuk Khaidhirah Abu Zahar, better known as Dira, will face PH candidate Esma Eazreen Husin, the Jasin division chief of the Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Women’s Wing.
Duyong will see a straight fight between incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem of BN and PH candidate Poo Long Suan, a member of the DAP Melaka Complaints Committee. In Merlimau, incumbent Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh of BN will be challenged by PH candidate Rahayu Hamzah.
Among the three-cornered contests, Machap Jaya will see incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem of BN face former assemblyman Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin of PH and B. Prasanth Kumar of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
In Paya Rumput, prime minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, representing PH, will face Rafie Ahmad of Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Bersama.
Bandar Hilir will see incumbent Leng Chau Yen of PH contest against BN candidate Jasmine Lok Huey Yee and Dr Mohd Nor Rashidi Ab Jalil of Bersama.
Meanwhile, Bukit Katil and Ayer Keroh will each see four-cornered contests.
In Bukit Katil, incumbent and Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari will face PN candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif, Bersama candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
In Ayer Keroh, incumbent Kerk Chee Yee of PH will be challenged by Datuk Seri Michael Gan Peng Lam of PN, Mohd Hamnaim Mohamad of Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) and Muhammad Muhaimin Lau Abdullah of Bersama.
The 28-seat Melaka State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on September 23 with the consent of Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 10 for early voting and November 14 as polling day.
A total of 687,697 voters are eligible to cast their ballots, comprising 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
In the 15th Melaka State Election on November 20, 2021, BN won 21 seats, with UMNO securing 18, MCA two and MIC one, enabling the coalition to form the state government with a more than two-thirds majority.
PH won five seats, with DAP securing four and Amanah one, while PN won two.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Amanah vs Umno in Merlimau: Rahayu knows Dr Akmal is big on social media, so she’s counting on voters at the grassroots
Article:
JASIN, Oct 31 — A father’s advice to always remain strong and broad-minded has inspired Melaka Amanah Wanita chief Rahayu Hamzah to take on the challenge of contesting the Merlimau state seat for Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the 16th Melaka state election.
She said the advice had become her guiding principle, particularly as she prepares to face Barisan Nasional (BN) incumbent Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh.
Acknowledging Dr Muhamad Akmal’s strong social media influence as Umno Youth chief, Rahayu said she remained confident of PH’s support among voters in the constituency.
“We recognise his social media influence, but we are prepared. I believe in the support of voters on the ground, and that is why I am ready to take on this challenge,” she told reporters here today.
Rahayu said that if elected, she would focus on serving the community in line with PH’s Melaka Rumah Kita aspirations, with education for young people among her priorities.
She also pledged to address local infrastructure concerns, including flooding, based on residents’ needs and complaints.
Meanwhile, Dr Muhamad Akmal said he was not targeting a large majority in Merlimau but instead sought voters’ confidence based on his service over the past four years and 11 months.
“If they feel my service has not been good, I honestly say they should not vote for me. But if they are satisfied with my performance, I ask for their trust once again,” he said.
Dr Muhamad Akmal said he was prepared to face criticism and allegations from his opponents during the campaign, adding that voters were capable of assessing the information presented to them.
He also urged all campaign teams to conduct their activities maturely and responsibly, and to refrain from provocation, slander and remarks intended to discredit others.
The Merlimau seat will see a straight fight between Dr Muhamad Akmal and Rahayu.
Polling day is set for November 14, while early voting will take place on November 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Three or four checks, then one big raid: How a Puchong chicken warehouse that flouted halal rules ran for 20 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A chicken slaughtering and processing warehouse in Puchong, raided under Ops Taring Chiller yesterday, is believed to have operated for 20 years.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence and Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said investigations identified the warehouse owner as a 34-year-old local man.
“Check results showed this fresh chicken slaughtering and processing warehouse has operated for roughly 20 years.
“Investigations also revealed that the warehouse owner is a 34-year-old local man, and further investigations into the matter will be continued by the Halal Enforcement Division of the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais),” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
He added that during the warehouse’s operation, Jais and relevant enforcement agencies conducted three to four raids and inspections. Yesterday’s raid was the first involving the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) via WCB/PSK.
Mohd Zaki, in a statement yesterday, confirmed that authorities seized over 6.5 tonnes of chicken suspected to have been processed without adhering to Syariah-compliant slaughtering methods and halal certification requirements during the raid on the warehouse in Puchong.
Also detained in Ops Taring Chiller were 12 Bangladeshi and Pakistani men believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing activities at the premises.
The live chicken supply is believed to have been sourced from several poultry farms around Sepang. The processed chicken was distributed to customers including eateries, grocery stores, and supermarkets across the Klang Valley.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1)(A) and Section 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011, as well as Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: PSK stands for Perisikan dan Siasatan Khas in Malay. Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, and PDRM stands for Polis Diraja Malaysia.
