Title: Too soon to count? PSD hasn’t measured Waze ban compliance yet
Article:
KAMPAR, Oct 31 — The Public Service Department (JPA) is confident that civil servants will fully comply with the ban on the use of the Waze navigation application.
Director-General of Public Service (KPPA) Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the compliance rate among civil servants had yet to be determined, as the government had only recently announced the directive.
Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that civil servants would take the matter seriously and comply with the ban, which was imposed for security reasons.
“Civil servants are no longer allowed to use Waze due to security concerns. We have also learned from what happened to other countries that used the application,” he said after officiating at the closing ceremony of the Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani JPA programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Kota Baharu here today.
On October 21, the government decided to ban all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application to protect government information and users’ personal data from the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the decision took into account the fact that Waze Mobile Ltd, which controls user data, is incorporated and operates under Israeli law.
Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Dahlan said RM1.465 million had been allocated to improve infrastructure, upgrade public facilities and support educational programmes under the Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani programme for residents of Kampung Kota Bharu and students of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Malim Nawar here.
He said RM500,000 from the Ministry of Finance and an additional RM35,000 from JPA were set aside for eight physical projects under the Kampung Angkat Madani initiative, including upgrades to the mosque, community hall, health clinic, police station and pavilion at SK Kota Baharu, as well as the construction of a village landmark and the provision of smart boards.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also said collaboration with the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development had resulted in the installation of 40 solar-powered streetlights worth RM380,000, while the Implementation Coordination Unit under the Prime Minister’s Department had allocated RM450,000 for the construction of a new multipurpose hall with two badminton courts.
He said an allocation of RM90,000 was also provided to SMK Malim Nawar to upgrade its computer laboratory, Design and Technology workshop and science laboratories, with another RM10,000 earmarked for educational development programmes for students and teachers.
“Various community and educational activities have also been held, including a korban programme, GP Joran fishing competition, traditional games, health and psychological outreach programme, Tuisyen Madani, gotong-royong activities and Wira Komuniti Carnival,” he said.
The closing ceremony also saw 97 families in Kampung Kota Bharu receive Bakul Rahmah aid, while schools received contributions and JPA’s strategic partners were recognised for their support.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also praised the SK Kota Baharu team for winning a gold medal for its Ecowire Roll innovation at the International Innovation and Entrepreneurship Expo 2026 on October 25.
He also highlighted the achievement of a female student from SMK Malim Nawar who was selected to represent Selangor in football.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said these achievements showed that children from rural areas could excel when given the right opportunities, facilities and support. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JPA stands for Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam in Malay, also known as PSD in English, while KPPA stands for Ketua Pengarah Perkhidmatan Awam in Malay.

Title: Sabah is short of nearly 245 medical officers, and Ranau Hospital feels it most
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 31 — Sabah is facing a shortage of nearly 245 medical officers following the implementation of the Phase 2 Permanent Appointment exercise on September 28, with Ranau Hospital among the healthcare facilities affected by the transfer of existing medical officers.
The Sabah State Health Department (Sabah JKN) said the shortage was partly due to 67 per cent of replacement candidates from outside Sabah failed to report for duty after accepting offers of permanent appointment, hindering efforts to fill vacancies in the state.
Ranau Hospital is currently operating with only nine medical officers, including the hospital director, after 11 of its 19 medical officers were transferred out under the exercise.
“Although the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) identified seven replacement officers from outside Sabah, only one has reported for duty,” the department said in a statement today.
It said the situation at Ranau Hospital reflected a broader shortage of medical officers across Sabah, with several other healthcare facilities facing similar challenges.
As an immediate measure, Sabah JKN will deploy three temporary relief medical officers, or ‘floater’ officers, to Ranau Hospital in stages, beginning on October 28 and November 11.
Meanwhile, the MOH will conduct a special permanent appointment exercise for Grade UD10 medical officers to meet the staffing needs of healthcare services in Sabah and Sarawak.
Sabah JKN said the placement of medical officers under the special exercise, with reporting for duty, was expected to begin as early as February 2027.
The department reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring the continuity of essential medical services while taking proactive measures to address the shortage of medical officers in the state. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JKN stands for Jabatan Kesihatan Negeri in Malay.

Title: Brothers on opposite sides: Akmal Salleh's sibling stands for Bersama in Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Dr Muhammad Solehin Saleh, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, is among 16 Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidates contesting the Melaka state election.
Muhammad Solehin, 40, is representing the party in the Bemban state seat under the Jasin parliamentary constituency in a four-cornered fight,
Sinar Harian
reported.
He will face Muhammad Rabaie Ab Hamid of Bersatu, Mohd Yadzil Yaakub of PN-Wawasan and independent candidate Abd Halim Said.
Muhammad Solehin is a medical doctor with a Bachelor of General Medicine from Universitas Sriwijaya, Indonesia.
Meanwhile, Akmal is defending the Merlimau seat for Barisan Nasional (BN) in a straight fight against Pakatan Harapan’s Rahayu Hamzah of Amanah.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Akmal retained the seat for Umno-BN with a majority of 3,248 votes.
He was later appointed state executive councillor in charge of health before being moved to the rural development, agriculture and food security portfolio in 2023.

Title: Stolen Hilux leads cops to syndicate behind eight 4x4 thefts in Perak and KL
Article:
SITIAWAN, Oct 31 — Police have crippled a syndicate believed to be involved in stealing four-wheel-drive vehicles in Perak and Kuala Lumpur with the arrest of three people in Kampung Koh here on Tuesday.
Manjung district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hasbullah Abd Rahman said the arrests were made following information and intelligence gathered after a report on the theft of a Toyota Hilux in Taman Mas 2, Sitiawan, on Oct 26.
He said the Manjung district police headquarters received the report at about 10.06am that day.
“Following the report, a team from the Manjung district police headquarters arrested a man and two women suspected of being involved in the incident on Oct 27 at about 5.30pm.
“Police also seized a car key reader believed to have been used to steal vehicles, as well as several other items,” he said in a statement today,
Sinar Harian r
eported.
Hasbullah said questioning revealed the suspects had admitted to being involved in eight vehicle thefts using the same modus operandi, targeting four-wheel-drive vehicles.
He said four of the cases were reported in Perak and the other four in Kuala Lumpur.
According to the report, the case is being investigated under Section 379A of the Penal Code for motor vehicle theft, and all three suspects have been remanded for six days from Oct 28 to Nov 2.
Members of the public with information on the case are urged to come forward to the Manjung district police headquarters, contact its operations room at 05-688 6222, reach its WhatsApp hotline at 017-682 8005, or visit any nearby police station.

Title: Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir: MCA takes on DAP’s home turf
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Two additional state assembly seats to be contested by MCA candidates in the 16th Melaka state election, namely Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, pose a significant challenge for the party to secure the people’s mandate in the state, especially from the Chinese community.
MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said it serves as a platform to gauge public support for the party because the majority of voters in both constituencies are Chinese, and these seats have been dominated by the DAP for several terms.
Wee, who is also the Ayer Hitam member of parliament and a former transport minister, said that the Melaka state election is likened to a referendum to assess the people’s support for the Pakatan Harapan government, which has been governing the country for almost four years.
“We realise that it is not easy to conquer the two DAP strongholds, but we will work hard to gain the people’s mandate in these areas.
“We will make the best use of this opportunity by mobilising our efforts and machinery to gain the support of the voters,” he said after accompanying the Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the Kelebang state constituency, Datuk Lim Ban Hong, to the Nomination Centre at the State
Legislative Assembly Development and Coordination Committee Complex (Japerun).
Commenting on BN’s decision to grant the two additional seats to MCA, Wee said they appreciated the trust and support of the BN leadership as well as the views of the Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders who deemed MCA suitable to contest and potentially win in those areas.
He said the MCA always pays attention to the people of Melaka, including all the state assembly constituencies under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency, even though the area is a stronghold of the DAP.
Meanwhile, he is confident that Lim can retain the Kelebang state assembly seat based on his excellent service record and good relationship with the local community, despite facing a rather intense four-cornered contest.
“We will continue to work hard to ensure that every vote from the people of Kelebang can be secured, thereby strengthening the position of the MCA,” he also said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, while the nomination of candidates is today and early voting is on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: Japerun stands for Jawatankuasa Pembangunan dan Penyelarasan Dewan Undangan Negeri in Malay.

Title: Pakatan has both ends of the age scale covered: A 24-year-old law grad and a retired captain, 66
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The youngest candidate in the 16th Melaka state election, Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah, will contest the Kuala Linggi state seat.
Representing Pakatan Harapan (PH), the 24-year-old from Parti Amanah and a law graduate of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia faces a three-cornered fight for the seat.
He will be challenged by incumbent Datuk Rosli Abdullah of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Dr Nur Farhana Hamzah of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
In the 2021 Melaka polls, PH’s Farzana Hayani Nasir set the youngest-candidate record, at 21.
Kuala Linggi is one of five state seats under the Masjid Tanah parliamentary constituency, with 15,483 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots this time around.
Meanwhile, Capt (Rtd) Mohamad Jaafar, 66, also representing PH, is the oldest candidate in this election, contesting the Telok Mas seat against incumbent Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman of BN and Muhammad Hazwan Mustafa of Bersama.
The oldest candidate in the previous polls was Datuk Kalsom Noordin, 68, who contested the Pengkalan Batu seat on a BN ticket.
Telok Mas is one of five state seats under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency, with 29,751 eligible registered voters.
Of the 79 candidates in this election, 14 are women, a slight decline from the previous election, which saw 16 women among 112 candidates, with PH fielding the most female candidates at six.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Capt (Rtd) stands for Captain (Retired), or Kapten (Bersara) in Malay. Amanah is the short name for Parti Amanah Negara.

Title: Child, 10, among 181 detained in Chow Kit immigration raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The Immigration Department detained 181 foreign nationals for various immigration offences during an integrated operation at Jalan Raja Bot, or Chow Kit Market, here this morning.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said the operation began at 9.40 am and involved checks on 512 foreign nationals.
“A total of 181 foreign nationals were detained for various immigration offences, including lacking valid travel documents, overstaying, and pass misuse,” he told reporters at the scene today.
He said those detained included 147 Indonesians, 20 Bangladeshis, five Nepalese, three Indians, one Pakistani and five others from various countries, aged between 10 and 55. All detainees were brought to the Bukit Jalil Immigration Depot for further action.
The integrated operation also involved Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN), the National Registration Department, the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department and the Royal Malaysia Police.
Lokman Effendi said Raja Bot Market is among 224 hotspots nationwide under continuous monitoring by the authorities.
He said this was the second operation at the location this year after intelligence gathering to determine the right time for an enforcement operation.
Operations will continue if immigration law violations persist, and no area will be exempt from enforcement, he said.
He added that enforcement actions are not limited to foreign nationals, as employers and premises owners who break the law will also face legal consequences.
“We remind employers not to commit any offences under the Immigration Act, as they will also be liable to legal action under this Act.
“Locals attempting to assist these foreign nationals can also be acted against, as harbouring undocumented foreign nationals in our country constitutes an offence,” he said.
Lokman Effendi said foreign nationals legally residing in the country need not worry, as enforcement operations target only those who violate the law. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: DBKL stands for Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur in Malay, while KPDN stands for Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup.

Title: Police arrest 16 foreigners in raid on Jalan Ampang hotel penthouse ‘mini casino’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police have detained 16 foreign nationals after raiding a hotel penthouse on Jalan Ampang where a “mini casino” was operating.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Fadil Marsus said the raid was carried out at 1.50am today, according to a
Free Malaysia Today
report.
“An investigation found that the penthouse was being used as a mini casino open only to close acquaintances, involving Chinese nationals only,” he said in a statement.
Those arrested comprised 15 Chinese nationals, including one woman, and a Nepali, all aged between 26 and 50.
Police seized 214 poker chips valued at RM5,180 in total, along with RM1,000 in cash.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act, the Common Gaming Houses Act and Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing public servants.
The suspects are due to be brought to the magistrates’ court today for remand.

Title: Same fix as 2023, please: Indian civil servants ask Putrajaya to add Nov 10 as extra Deepavali day
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 31 — The Putrajaya Indian Civil Servants Association (Imaiyam) is appealing to the government to grant unrecorded leave (CTR) to Hindu civil servants on Tuesday, November 10, as this year’s Deepavali leave overlaps with a public holiday and its replacement holiday.
Imaiyam chairman Dr Sathiskumar K. Muthusamy said the request is not aimed at securing a new benefit, but at ensuring that the existing Deepavali CTR, long provided by the government, can be fully enjoyed by Hindu civil servants.
“Deepavali this year falls on a Sunday, and Monday has been declared a replacement holiday. As a result, the day usually used for CTR overlaps with the public holiday, and the benefit cannot be enjoyed,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
“Our request is simple: that the CTR be allowed on Tuesday, November 10. The government made the same decision in 2023 under similar circumstances. We are confident it will remain consistent with that approach,” he said.
Dr Sathiskumar said the Deepavali CTR is already governed by the Human Resource Service Circular (MyPPSM); therefore, the Public Service Department (JPA) only needs to issue a circular letter allowing the CTR to be carried over to the next working day, as was done in 2023.
He said the circular could also be extended to state public services, statutory bodies and local authorities to ensure coordinated implementation.
Imaiyam has received questions and feedback from members about the limited time available during the Deepavali break, particularly among civil servants working far from their hometowns, including in Sabah and Sarawak.
“With only one replacement holiday, the time to return to one’s hometown, celebrate with family and return to work is very limited,” he said, adding that the matter has been brought to JPA’s attention.
Imaiyam stressed that fairness must underpin the consideration of festive leave for all civil servants regardless of religion or race.
If existing festive leave for followers of other religions is similarly affected by overlaps with public or replacement holidays, the same approach should be considered.
Since 2018, the government has provided one day of CTR for Deepavali, on the following day, to Hindu civil servants as an addition to the public holiday, giving them more room to celebrate with their families. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: CTR stands for Cuti Tanpa Rekod, MyPPSM refers to Pekeliling Perkhidmatan Sumber Manusia, and JPA stands for Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam in Malay.

Title: Among the youngest in the race, Pakatan’s Nana says Kelebang needs a voice for women and young people
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Undeterred by her defeat in her first electoral contest in Sungai Rambai, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir is once again throwing her hat into the ring in the 16th Melaka state election.
The 26-year-old Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate, affectionately known as Nana, said her unsuccessful electoral debut at 21 had been a valuable learning experience, giving her renewed confidence to contest the Kelebang state seat.
The Tangga Batu Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief said the experience had also given her a better understanding of the challenges involved, allowing her to prepare more effectively this time around.
“What I learnt from my first election has really helped me prepare for Kelebang. Alhamdulillah, we’re much more organised this time, especially with our schedules and campaign machinery,” she told reporters after the nomination process at the Klebang State Legislative Assembly Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) Complex here today.
The Bukit Rambai native said she remained determined to give her best for voters in the constituency despite being the youngest candidate in a four-cornered contest.
Farzana Hayani said she would use the 14-day campaign period to champion women’s issues, while also focusing on the needs of the fishing community and job opportunities for young people.
“I understand the challenges of being a mother, a wife and a working woman. I also know how difficult it can be for young women who have to live apart from their husbands because of work,” she said.
Meanwhile, Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Lim Ban Hong said he was taking nothing for granted in the state election despite being the incumbent Kelebang assemblyman.
The Melaka MCA chairman said he had never stopped working for his constituents and remained committed to serving the local community.
“This state election gives me another opportunity to continue working for the people of Kelebang and do my best for them. I hope they will once again give me and BN the mandate to continue serving them,” he said.
Farzana Hayani and Lim will face off against Bersatu’s Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad and Parti Bersama Malaysia’s Young Jie Yu in the race for the Klebang state seat.
Polling day is set for November 14, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Japerun stands for Jawatankuasa Pembangunan dan Penyelarasan Dewan Undangan Negeri in Malay while AMK refers to the youth wing of PKR.

Title: Fahmi: Courier scams are everywhere, so let’s fight back with Parcel Shield
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — The government is intensifying efforts to protect consumers from fraud syndicates that exploit courier services and e-commerce platforms through the launch of Parcel Shield anti-fraud initiative today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative led by Postal Forum aims to increase consumer awareness and vigilance against various modus operandi of fraud related to parcel delivery, including impersonating courier companies, fake delivery notifications, phishing links and cash on delivery (COD) fraud.
He said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) together with courier companies would work together to intensify efforts to raise consumer awareness of the threat of fraud that uses fake parcel delivery tactics.
“The Communications Ministry and all courier companies will also expand this initiative through public service message services on radio and television to ensure that consumers, especially Malaysians, benefit from this initiative,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after launching the Parcel Shield initiative in conjunction with National Courier Day 2026 at the Selangor International Trade Centre today.
Also present were secretary-general of the Ministry of Communications Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, chief executive officer of Postal Forum Nurhafizah Hanifah and president of the Malaysian Express Delivery Companies Association Ronald Tan.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said 13,045 banned contents related to fraud, gambling and services were detected by e-commerce platforms from January 1 until yesterday.
He said the Cabinet in its meeting yesterday also agreed in principle with the proposed amendment to the Postal Services Act 2012 as one of the government’s steps to strengthen efforts to curb such activities, in addition to detailing the welfare aspects of courier workers.
“The approval we have obtained so far is at the policy level for the amendment and it will take several months to prepare the draft.
“So we estimate the process will take time because there are regulations that we need to comply with. But we expect it to be tabled in Parliament as early as mid- or late next year,” he said.
Fahmi said the amendment to the act also aims to ensure that the welfare and protection aspects of courier workers are given attention, in line with the government’s efforts to introduce the Postal Fund initiative which is scheduled to be launched in the first quarter of 2027.
In this regard, he will ask MCMC and the Communications Ministry to invite all licensed delivery companies to participate in the process of drafting amendments to the Postal Services Act 2012. — Bernama

Title: Let’s talk Machap Jaya’s future: Pakatan hopeful hands out invitation cards, Bersama candidate says yes, BN incumbent says now is time for work
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Machap Jaya seat, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, has invited her two opponents in the Melaka State Election to an open dialogue to discuss development plans for the constituency.
Lim, who won the seat in the 2018 state election, said the proposed dialogue was aimed at encouraging objective and constructive discussions rather than allowing the campaign to revolve around personal attacks and criticism of opponents.
“We hope to discuss how we can develop or make Machap a better place over the next five years. We want to move away from a style of politics that consists merely of shouting or badmouthing one another,” she told reporters after the nomination process for the Machap Jaya seat at the Machap Jaya Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) complex in Bukit Bulat today.
Earlier, she was seen handing invitation cards to the other two candidates for the seat, Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem of Barisan Nasional (BN) and B. Prasanth Kumar of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
Lim, a former state executive council (exco) member who held the portfolios of Women, Family Development, Welfare Affairs and Orang Asli Community, described her contest against incumbent Ngwe, also known as YB Sem, as a “friendly” rivalry, noting that both had experience serving in the state executive council.
Meanwhile, Ngwe said he had yet to decide whether to accept Lim’s invitation, as he needed to review his campaign schedule, adding that the current campaign period was not an appropriate time for such a dialogue.
“For me, now is the time for work, not dialogue. I am already aware of the people’s issues, having served for five years. It is not as if I am only now asking what needs to be done,” said Ngwe, who is the state exco for Health, Human Resources and Unity.
He said his five years as an elected representative, during which he had consistently engaged with residents and addressed their concerns, would stand him in good stead in defending the seat.
Prasanth Kumar, however, welcomed Lim’s invitation, describing the proposed dialogue as a useful platform for candidates to exchange ideas and proposals for the benefit of Machap Jaya residents.
“I believe this open dialogue is a good platform for us to pool our ideas. While each candidate may have different approaches, I am confident that everyone shares the same goal, to help the community in the Machap Jaya constituency,” said the law graduate.
Commenting on his contest against two former state executive councillors, Prasanth Kumar said that although Bersama was only five months old, he had considerable experience in politics and administration, having contested the Rim state seat in the previous state election.
He had also served as Special Secretary for Community Affairs to former Melaka Chief Minister Adly Zahari, and as an officer with special duties to former Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad.
Lim won the Machap Jaya seat in the 2018 state election with a majority of 1,336 votes, polling 5,550 votes in a three-cornered contest against Koh Nai Kwong of BN-MCA and Wan Zahidi Wan Ismail of PAS.
In the 2021 state election, Ngwe won the seat with 3,732 votes, defeating PH candidate Law Bing Haw by a 938-vote majority in a five-cornered contest. Lim did not contest in that election.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 10 for early voting and November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election.

Title: Rural, urban or both? PM’s pol sec Azman Abidin says Paya Rumput needs a bit of everything
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Paya Rumput state seat, Datuk Azman Abidin, is banking on his extensive experience and close ties with the federal government to better serve the constituency.
Speaking after submitting his nomination papers at Stadium Hang Jebat here today, he said Paya Rumput’s semi-urban setting required a comprehensive approach to address the needs of both rural and urban communities.
“I can offer my experience to assist residents, facilitate their affairs and address their needs.
“My experience serving alongside the prime minister, as well as my ties with the federal government, can be put to good use in addressing the issues faced by Paya Rumput residents,” he told reporters.
The prime minister’s political secretary said he did not underestimate any of his opponents, noting that every candidate had their own strengths.
His main focus during the campaign would be to reach as many voters as possible and explain the services and welfare initiatives he could offer.
Azman, 54, who holds a Professional Master of Business Administration (PMBA) from Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM), expressed confidence in voters’ openness to change.
He will be challenged by Rafie Ahmad of Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
Polling day is set for November 14, while early voting will take place on November 10.

Title: Adam Adli: Perikatan’s RoS suspension is their internal conflict, not Pakatan's doing
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan has dismissed suggestions that it engineered the Registrar of Societies’ move to suspend Perikatan Nasional, insisting the matter stems from troubles inside the opposition bloc.
Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim rejected the allegation outright and pushed back against Gerakan president Datuk Dr Dominic Lau’s assertion that the suspension carried a political motive, the
New Straits Times
reported.
“We reject these allegations. This has nothing to do with us. It is not our strategy, and we are not involved at all,” he said at a press conference at the PH main operations centre.
“That is their internal conflict,” he added.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman were also present.
Adam said that PH’s priority was a fair electoral contest that lets Melaka voters choose their next state government.
“We have made it clear that the election in Melaka is a democratic process to give voters the opportunity to decide who should form the state government,” he said.
“It has nothing to do with any disputes or political disagreements unrelated to the electoral process.”
Lau had alleged on Thursday that the RoS action formed part of a PH strategy ahead of the Melaka polls.
“Why was PN suspended only now? This is a malicious intent. This is a political decision, this is indeed PH’s agenda,” he was quoted as saying at PN’s candidate announcement event.
Lau further claimed the suspension was meant to ease Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s path to a second term, tying it to PKR’s Melaka congress on Aug 16.
PN secured reprieve on Oct 22 when the High Court stayed the RoS decision to revoke its registration, pending its judicial review application.
The court also halted enforcement of an RoS notice suspending PN’s activities, clearing the coalition to keep operating and to contest the Melaka election.
Adam said PH would spend the campaign promoting its candidates and policies.
He added that the coalition would shun personal attacks and divisive tactics, especially those aimed at younger candidates.
Polling for the Melaka election is set for Nov 14, with early voting on Nov 10.

Title: Stamp duty and e-Invoice amnesty windows are closing, IRB reminds taxpayers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The tax literacy programme implemented by the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (IRB) throughout the 2026 HASiL Month has involved nearly 300,000 taxpayers nationwide.
Its chief executive officer, Datuk Dr Abu Tariq Jamaluddin, said various programmes were implemented throughout October to raise public awareness of taxation and the agency’s role.
“During this period, we have conducted several activities, including the HASiL Literacy Tour, under which we have carried out 251 tours across the country to engage with communities and explain issues related to taxation,” he told reporters during the closing ceremony of the 2026 HASiL Month here today.
Abu Tariq noted that IRB also received nearly 50,000 responses through surveys to gather public opinions on taxation and the services provided by the agency.
He said the feedback included views collected this year as well as in previous years.
“Among the focuses of the 2026 HASiL Month is promoting the voluntary declaration programmes for stamp duty and e-Invoice, with the stamp duty programme ending at the end of this year and the e-Invoice programme at the end of next year,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said IRB also encourages the public to provide information about individuals or companies suspected of underreporting their taxes through the e-Tax Escape platform.
“The information we receive will be kept confidential,” he added. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: HASiL is the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia’s brand name. It comes from the Malay word “hasil”, meaning revenue, and is not a strict acronym. The board’s Malay name is Lembaga Hasil Dalam Negeri.

Title: Pakatan’s red line in Melaka: No hate, no incitement, no race-baiting
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has set its stance of not compromising and rejecting the politics of hatred, incitement and narrow racial narratives throughout the 16th Melaka state election campaign.
PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the coalition chose to highlight the campaign based on the theme ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’, focusing on competing ideas, service records and the welfare of the people.
Saifuddin Nasution, who is also the Home Minister, explained that victory in the election is not judged by which party is the most vocal in inciting hostility, but rather by which party is most trusted to be able to defend the fate of the community.
“Our red line is to completely reject the politics of hatred, the politics of incitement and politics that is based on the idea that to defend our race, we must oppress other races. For our race to succeed, other races have no place... we completely reject that.
“We will focus on a peaceful campaign, because we are convinced that an election campaign is not measured by the victory of which party is the loudest, but who is actually the most trusted and credible,” he said at a press conference at the PH Main Operations Room here today.
Commenting further, Saifuddin Nasution said the three main messages that PH brought in the election campaign this time were to celebrate the festival of democracy by respecting differences of opinion; to highlight policy offers and the ability to solve problems; and to launch a manifesto that focuses on job opportunities, the cost of living and the future of the youth.
Touching on the direction of the campaign, Saifuddin Nasution explained that PH would not entertain any political speculation regarding the new alignment after the election, but instead would focus fully on reaching out to voters including out-of-constituency voters.
“The out-of-constituency voter segment is indeed included in the electoral machinery’s checklist. We have accurate figures for each seat contested regarding out-of-constituency voters, and they are the focus of our attention to be contacted to ensure they return to vote,” he explained.
The EC has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka election while early voting is on November 10.

Title: Wi-Fi, laptops and a polyclinic: What Pakatan’s Adly Zahari wants to deliver in Bukit Katil
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Enhancing digital education facilities is among the key priorities of Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Bukit Katil state seat, Adly Zahari, should he be given the mandate in the 16th Melaka state election.
The incumbent said the effort was important to ensure that the younger generation in the constituency benefited from developments in digital technology, particularly in education, security and economic development.
“If I am given the mandate, my main focus will certainly be to improve digital education facilities for our children in the Bukit Katil state constituency, as well as for our entrepreneurs,” he told reporters after the nomination process at Dewan Tun Ali, Bukit Katil, here today.
The Amanah vice-president is facing a four-cornered contest against Perikatan Nasional (PN) candidate Ridzuan Sarif, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said digital education should be given priority, as a digitally literate generation could benefit the education sector while also contributing to stronger economic capabilities now and in the future.
He also said that completing the construction of a polyclinic in the constituency was another matter that needed attention.
“We have already obtained approval from the Ministry of Health (MOH), and we have secured the budget,” he said.
Commenting on the Melaka polls, Adly described the contest as one of the bigger challenges he had faced, with candidates from PN, Bersama and the independent camp also in the running.
However, he said his eight years of service in the Bukit Katil state constituency, including during the 22 months when PH was in government, provided a basis for voters to assess his track record.
“So, we (PH) leave it to the people to assess all the efforts we have made, and we will continue to serve them regardless of the outcome. We will certainly respect whatever decision the people make.
“However, we are appealing to the people to give us an opportunity to serve for a third term, and we are confident that our achievements will receive the support of voters in the Bukit Katil state constituency,” he said.
In the 15th Melaka state election, Adly secured a majority of 1,057 votes after defeating three other candidates, namely Datuk Hasnoor Sdg Husin of BN, Muhammad Al Afiz Yahya of PN and independent candidate Abdul Hamid.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10.

Title: Four bullet marks, one BMW in Sitiawan: Manjung police on the trail of motorcycle gunmen
Article:
IPOH, Oct 31 — Police are tracking down suspects involved in a shooting incident in which several shots were fired at a BMW in front of a house in Taman Hijau, Kampung Koh, near Sitiawan, yesterday.
Manjung police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said that police received a report from a man at 1.54 pm yesterday regarding the incident.
He said investigations revealed that the incident was believed to have occurred at 4.16 am on the same day, when the complainant, who was inside his house, heard what sounded like gunshots. The complainant later discovered about 9 am that there were four bullet marks on the right-side door of his vehicle.
“A review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at the scene showed two unidentified suspects approaching the vehicle on a motorcycle,” he said in a statement today.
“One of the suspects then fired shots at the vehicle before fleeing. Police have opened an investigation paper and the case is being investigated under Section 39 of the Arms Act 1960,” he said, adding that efforts to track down the suspects were ongoing.
Hasbullah said members of the public with any information on the incident were urged to come forward at the Manjung district police headquarters (IPD) or contact its Operations Room at 05-688 6222, the WhatsApp hotline at 017-682 8005, or any nearby police station.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, Hasbullah said police had arrested a man and two women, aged between 24 and 26, on suspicion of being involved in the theft of a Toyota Hilux belonging to a man in Taman Mas 2, Sitiawan.
He said the three suspects had been remanded for six days, from October 28 to November 2, to facilitate investigations under Section 379A of the Penal Code.
“At about 5.30 pm on October 27, a team of police personnel from the Manjung IPD arrested all three suspects, who were believed to be involved in the incident. Police also seized a car key reader device believed to have been used in the vehicle thefts, as well as several other items.
“Interrogations found that the suspects admitted to being involved in eight vehicle theft cases, four in Perak and four in Kuala Lumpur, using the same modus operandi and targeting four-wheel-drive vehicles,” he said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials IPD stands for Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah in Malay. Section 379A of the Penal Code concerns the theft of a motor vehicle or any of its component parts, and carries imprisonment of between one and seven years upon conviction, and the offender is also liable to a fine.

Title: It takes a village: Society plans RM25m place in Pahang for autistic adults with nowhere to go
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 31 — The National Autism Society of Malaysia plans to develop an autism village to provide safe accommodation for adult autistic individuals who have nowhere to live in Pahang.
The intention was expressed following the presence of the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah to officiate the society’s Kuantan 2026 Charity Sale Ceremony at Taman Gelora here, today.
The society’s patron Datuk Megat Ahmad Shahrani Megat Sharuddin said the proposed development of the village aimed to ensure that autistic individuals aged 30 to 50, especially those who no longer have guardians, received suitable accommodation and continuous care.
He said the centre was proposed to accommodate about 200 residents with an estimated development cost of about RM25 million based on a study conducted.
“When their parents are gone, some of them do not have siblings or family members to take the responsibility of caring for them. We want to provide a place so that they are not abandoned,” he told reporters after the event.
Megat Ahmad Shahrani said his party was trying to obtain five acres of land and hoped that the proposal would receive the attention and support of the Pahang Royal Institution to realise the wish.
He said Pahang also had the potential to become a settlement for autistic individuals from all over the country and not just those from the state.
“The society is also trying to obtain financial support from corporate companies and related bodies to finance the project, but providing land is the main requirement before fundraising efforts can be intensified,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said the operating costs of the society’s centres nationwide reached about RM7 million a year, while the collection obtained was only around RM4 million, causing the association to have to find an additional RM3 million every year.
He said the cost of providing education and therapy for individuals with autism was high because the learning approach required more specific attention, with a low teacher-to-student ratio to ensure that the needs of each individual could be met.
“The society, however, strives to ensure that the fees charged remain affordable for all levels of society, in addition to providing assistance to underprivileged families based on an assessment of their circumstances,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Miri police nab four men linked to online loan sharks after red-paint attacks at borrowers’ homes
Article:
MIRI, Oct 31 — Four men have been arrested by Miri police in connection with paint-splashing vandalism cases linked to illegal online moneylending activities in the division.
Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement late Friday that the suspects were detained in four separate operations conducted in Kampung Pujut Tanjong Batu on October 23 and 26.
He said the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of Miri District Police Headquarters (IPD Miri) initially received a police report at 3.11pm on October 22 from a 54-year-old local man regarding an incident in which red paint was splashed on the front gate and porch floor of his house in Miri.
According to the complainant, the act was believed to be connected to demands for repayment of an online loan allegedly taken by his son.
The complainant discovered the incident around 10pm on October 21, after reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at his residence in Jalan Acorus 7 here.
“The footage showed two unidentified men arriving at the house before one of them splashed red paint on the front gate and the floor at the front of the house.
“Prior to the incident, the complainant had received messages from an individual using the name ‘Kelvin’, demanding repayment of an online loan allegedly taken by his son. The messages also contained threats should the payment not be made,” said Mohd Farhan.
Based on the complainant’s information, his son had previously borrowed money online from an individual believed to be involved in unlicensed moneylending activities. Although the earlier debt was said to have been settled, his son later informed him that he had taken another RM200 loan from a different online lender.
“Acting on intelligence and the findings of investigations, a team of CID officers from IPD Miri arrested four local men aged between 25 and 32.
“Police investigations found that all four suspects were involved in the reported paint-splashing vandalism cases, enabling police to solve two cases reported on October 20 and October 22,” he said.
Following the arrests, police seized several items from the suspects, including mobile phones, clothing, slippers, two helmets allegedly worn during the incidents and two motorcycles believed to have been used in the incidents.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code, which carries a penalty of one to five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Mohd Farhan said police take seriously any acts of intimidation, criminal mischief and threats that could jeopardise public safety and order.
He advised the public not to entertain threats or suspicious demands related to online loans and to lodge a police report immediately if they became victims or had information regarding such activities. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: The initials IPD stands for Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah in Malay.

Title: ‘Likes’ don’t fix roads, says Pakatan’s Duyong hopeful Poo Long Suan
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — As social media increasingly shapes politics, Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Duyong state seat, Poo Long Suan, believes meeting voters in person matters more than online popularity.
He said face-to-face interactions offered a better opportunity to understand the needs and concerns of the community, regardless of advances in technology.
While acknowledging the importance of social media presence, Poo, who is contesting against incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, said an elected representative’s primary responsibility was to serve the people through direct engagement on the ground.
“An assemblyman’s main responsibility is to serve the people. While having a social media presence is important nowadays, I believe meeting the people in person is far more important,” he told reporters after the nomination process at Dewan Kompleks Japerun Duyong here today.
The 43-year-old said he would draw on his experience, knowledge and achievements as a former Hang Tuah Jaya Municipal Council member to serve the people of Duyong.
Poo, who is also a member of the Melaka DAP Complaints Committee, acknowledged that improving residents’ well-being would take time, particularly as several aspects of local development still required attention.
He identified infrastructure, economic development and traffic management as key areas that could be further improved to enhance residents’ convenience and quality of life.
“Previous representatives have done a good job, but there is still room to improve the infrastructure, economy and traffic situation in Duyong,” he said.
Polling day is set for November 14, with early voting on November 10.
